s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive gluteal swelling with mild erythema
salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 32-year-old woman
1-year history of swelling
Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration performed with no fluid obtained
Surgical excision of a 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass
Mass was complex and septated, adherent to subcutaneous fat

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a slow-growing, painless mass near the gluteal cleft is consistent with an epidermoid cyst

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to epidermoid cyst, dermoid cysts can present as slow-growing, painless masses and are a plausible diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the mass

shortlist.label: Pilomatricoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pilomatricoma is a type of skin tumor that can present as a slow-growing, painless mass, and its location near the gluteal cleft makes it a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lipoma is a common type of benign tumor that can occur in the subcutaneous tissue, and its presence near the gluteal cleft is consistent with the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, teratomas can occur in the gluteal region and present as a slow-growing, painless mass, making it a rare but plausible diagnosis
